We propose a novel deep learning framework that integrates Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) and Gradient Boosting Machines (GBMs) to accurately predict global ammonia (NH3) emissions from croplands. This model will utilize a multi-source data approach, incorporating high-resolution satellite imagery, temporally synchronized soil sensor readings (focusing on pH, moisture, and temperature), and detailed agronomic practices (including specific OCA strategies such as types and amounts of manure applied). The CNN will focus on feature extraction from satellite images to capture spatial patterns of agricultural practices, while the GBM will handle the resulting processed features alongside direct sensor inputs to predict NH3 emissions.

Advanced feature selection techniques, including Shapley Additive Explanations (SHAP) and recursive feature elimination, will guide the identification of key drivers influencing NH3 emissions and crop productivity, enabling transparency in model predictions. Model validation will be rigorously executed through a cross-validation framework, utilizing a historical dataset encompassing multiple geographical regions and a diverse range of climatic conditions to ensure robustness.

The implications of this research extend to policy-making and agricultural practice, targeting sustainable development goals by providing actionable insights for farmers and environmental regulators on effective NH3 mitigation strategies while maintaining food security.
